title: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in Cotton & Pink Bollworm Management
source: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur
region: Central and Southern Cotton Growing Zones (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana, Karnataka)
content: Cotton faces major threats from sucking pests (jassids, aphids, thrips, whitefly) in early stages and Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) in reproductive stage. Cultural control: Terminate crop by December-January to break pink bollworm life cycle; avoid extending crop to 8-10 months. Install pheromone traps @ 5/ha for monitoring and @ 20-25/ha for mass trapping / mating disruption at 45 DAS. Economic Threshold Level (ETL) for Pink Bollworm: 8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive days or 10% rosette flowers / green boll damage. Early sucking pest control: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70 WS @ 5g/kg seed or Thiamethoxam 70 WS @ 4g/kg seed. Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) at 45-60 DAS. Biological control: Release Trichogramma bactrae egg parasitoid @ 1,50,000/ha at weekly intervals starting 60 DAS (3-4 releases). Chemical intervention (strictly based on ETL): If green boll rosette flowers exceed 10%, spray Profenofos 50 EC @ 2 ml/litre or Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG @ 0.4 g/litre. Precaution: Never spray synthetic pyrethroids before 90-100 DAS as it causes massive whitefly and mite resurgence.
